A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable and describe the same Vireo framework, with directly matching methods and main experiments. Inspection includes v1's scientific appendices and v3's concluding checklist; the missing scientific supplement is a document difference, not an extraction gap.

before.justification: Sections 4.3–4.4 report original segmentation results and component/backbone ablations. The appendices additionally report AustinScapes predictions, per-class results, efficiency measurements, and visual analyses.

after.justification: V3 retains the original benchmark results and ablations in Tables 1–6, together with segmentation, attention, feature-space, and training-loss visualizations.

M1.justification: The frozen visual, depth, and text encoders, cross-modal refinement, CMPE, and DOV-VEH retain the same procedures. GeoText Prompts becomes GeoText Query, but the equations and component operations do not establish an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: V3 removes the additional AustinScapes zero-shot evaluation from v1 Appendix A and Figure 8, losing an Austin street-scene target domain. The eight main benchmarks and their segmentation tasks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Supplementary comparisons disappear, including HGFormer in the GTA5-to-real qualitative comparison in Figure 10 and the efficiency comparison against SED, CAT-Seg, FC-CLIP, EBSeg, and REIN in Table 9. Comparator membership in retained Tables 1–6 is unchanged.

E3.justification: The separate efficiency evaluation in v1 Table 9, covering training time, memory, FPS, inference time, and mIoU averaged across ACDC, BDD100K, and Mapillary, is omitted. The retained experiments preserve their transfer configurations, data counts, mIoU metric, optimizer, 40,000-iteration budget, and batch size; no revised execution settings are established.

E4.justification: Removing Appendix C eliminates substantial supplementary analysis of small and rare categories, computational efficiency, close-up segmentation errors, and additional attention/affinity examples in Figures 9–13. The main component and backbone ablations, t-SNE visualization, and attention analysis remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. V3's checklist says the dataset protocols do not require error bars, but adds no uncertainty estimates or statistical procedure despite answering Yes to the significance question.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6 retain their numerical results. However, v3 removes Tables 7–8's per-class IoUs, Table 9's efficiency outcomes, including Vireo's reported 1.49 FPS, and supplementary qualitative results. This substantially reduces the reported evidence without establishing any same-setting performance change.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5 and their mathematical definitions remain equivalent. The new opening problem statement restates the existing image-and-class-label segmentation task; neither it nor the checklist adds a theorem, proof, or substantive derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims of a first unified single-stage OV-DGSS framework, the same three components, faster convergence, and superior cross-domain/open-vocabulary performance. The terminology change does not alter these contributions.

C2.justification: The omitted appendix removes discussion acknowledging Vireo's slower training/inference tradeoff, interpreting small/rare-category performance, and explaining affinity maps through within-object long-range dependencies. Main-text mechanism interpretations and the reliable-RGB-camera limitation remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The stated code repository changes from an anonymous account to SY-Ch/Vireo. AustinScapes collection/annotation information and supplementary compute-cost details disappear, while Section 4.2's implementation, hyperparameters, GPU, and training-budget disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 removes Appendix B's detailed OVSS/DGSS survey and nine distinct cited works, including discussions of ZSSeg, OpenSeg, X-Decoder, GroupViT, OpenSeeD, and BlindNet. The brief main related-work section remains. The additional Depth Anything V2 reference duplicates an already cited work.

P1.justification: The scientific appendices A–C and their detailed exposition are replaced by a NeurIPS checklist, substantially changing the document structure. Main-text edits are limited: terminology changes, an expanded methodology opening, title/affiliation updates, and added acknowledgements.

P2.justification: Tables 7–9 and Figures 8–13 disappear, removing per-class tables, the efficiency table, and extensive segmentation/attention panels rather than relocating them. Main displays largely retain their arrangement, with GeoText labels updated in Figures 2 and 5 and limited formatting changes.

improvement.justification: V3 preserves the headline claims and scores but removes the scientific supplement, including the only FPS/inference-time comparison, detailed classwise diagnostics, AustinScapes evaluation, and substantial research context. This substantially reduces empirical transparency and scrutiny of the robustness and efficiency claims. The clearer problem statement and updated code pointer offer limited benefits. Some removed reporting was internally inconsistent, notably Table 9 versus its timing/FPS discussion, but v3 supplies no corrected replacement analysis.
